newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh leader to clamp down on vodka smugglers.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh leader to clamp down on vodka smugglers.

text.p: Kazakhstan President Nursultan Nazarbayev, determined to clamp down on alcohol smugglers, said on Monday he wanted to place state controls on vodka production.
Nazarbayev told a news conference that 40 to 50 percent of wines and spirits for sale in the former Soviet republic, five times the size of France, were contraband.
He said the authorities had confiscated 1.62 million litres of smuggled alcohol in the last quarter of 1996.
Nazarbayev, the country's former Communist Party boss, said state controls did not mean that vodka producers faced nationalisation.
After more than two centuries of Tsarist and Soviet rule, vodka is drunk with as much abandon by the Moslem Kazakhs as their Russian neighbours to the north.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin ordered similar measures last week, clamping strict state control on production and sales of alcohol.
